samples.summary: `--fresh` deletes the rounds BEFORE the new bound refusal runs, so a refused run still destroys the carry-forward and the bound is bypassed by simply re-running
samples.evidence: In `cmdReview`, the delete loop `if (args.fresh && !dryRun) { for (const name of roundDirsToClear(readdirSync(base))) rmSync(...) }` (lines 954-958) executes BEFORE the bound decision at lines 974-983. On a real (non-dry) run with MAX rounds on disk, `spec-to-pr review --fresh` therefore: (1) removes every `round-N` directory, then (2) exits 1 with "past the self-review bound" — a command that reports it did nothing has already deleted the verdicts the message says must not be discarded. Worse, the state it measured is now gone: the very next invocation (with or without `--fresh`) sees `roundsOnDisk(base) === []`, so `onDiskBefore` is empty, `spentRound` is 1, `roundBoundNotice(1)` is "", and the round runs without `--force`. The new guard is thus defeated deterministically in one retry, which is exactly the "a fourth round presents itself as a clean first one" failure the comment at lines 967-973 claims to close. The added test only exercises `--dry-run` (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:657-700), where the delete is skipped, so this path is uncovered. Fix: compute `notice`/`spentRound` and refuse before performing the `--fresh` deletion.

samples.summary: An explicit `--round N` still walks past the bound without `--force`, and clobbers an existing round's verdicts
samples.evidence: `const round = args.round === undefined ? nextRound(onDisk) : Number(args.round);` (line 966) and, without `--fresh`, `spentRound = round` (line 974). So after 3 spent rounds, `review --round 1` yields `spentRound = 1`, `roundBoundNotice(1) === ""`, and the run proceeds unforced — the same "renumber past the gate" hole the delta just closed for `--fresh`. It additionally writes into the existing `round-1` directory (`mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })`, line 1012), overwriting that round's `pr.diff`/`verdict.json`s that a later round would have carried forward. Measuring the bound against `Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore))` in all cases, not just under `--fresh`, would close it.

samples.summary: `roundsOnDisk`'s new never-throws guard covers the inner readdir only; the outer `readdirSync(base)` still throws
samples.evidence: The added docblock (lines 801-810) states the guard exists so `priorFindingsFor`'s "never throws" contract cannot be broken from underneath, but only the per-round `readdirSync(dir, …)` is wrapped (lines 815-817). Line 812's `readdirSync(base)` is unguarded and throws ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EACCES if `base` is missing, is a plain file, or becomes unreadable between the guard checks and this call — propagating out of `priorFindingsFor` (line 840) as an uncaught stack rather than the "carry fewer findings" fail direction the module documents everywhere else.

samples.summary: New ancestor-ownership rule can refuse legitimate setups where an ancestor is owned by a non-root system account
samples.evidence: `if (!leaf && … stat.uid !== uid && stat.uid !== 0) return "it is owned by uid …"` in `unsafeBaseReason` rejects ANY ancestor not owned by root or the current uid, sticky bit and mode notwithstanding. That is the same class of over-broad ownership rule the comment at lines 526-531 says already "refused every run on macOS" once: environments where `os.tmpdir()`/`--out` sits below a directory owned by a system account other than uid 0 (some distro/NFS root-squash or container setups where root maps to a non-zero uid) now hard-fail every `review` invocation with no override flag. Worth confirming against the platforms this command claims to support.

The `--fresh` delete loop (spec-to-pr.mjs:954-958) runs before the bound decision (:974-983), and `fail` (:135-138) exits the process, so a refused non-dry `spec-to-pr review --fresh` with MAX rounds on disk deletes every round-N directory and then exits 1 claiming it ran nothing — destroying the carry-forward verdicts the message says must not be discarded (data loss). Worse, the measured state is gone: the next invocation sees an empty base, so `nextRound([]) === 1` (:180-186) and `roundBoundNotice(1) === ""` (:228-236), and the round runs without `--force`, deterministically bypassing the new bound. The added test (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:702-744) passes `--dry-run` on every invocation (:718), the one mode where `args.fresh && !dryRun` skips the delete, so the real path is uncovered.

finding.summary: The per-branch round directory is keyed on `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, which is the literal string `HEAD` in a detached HEAD — so every detached checkout shares one round counter and one carry-forward store.
finding.evidence: `cmdReview` (line 808) reads `branch = git(["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"])` and feeds it to `reviewBase(branch)` (line 723-727), which hashes that string into `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review/<safe>-<hash>`. In a detached HEAD — mid-rebase, `git bisect`, and notably the default `actions/checkout` state in CI (the docs added in this diff say CI is one of the two supported modes: "CI pins `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from repository secrets") — `--abbrev-ref HEAD` returns the string `HEAD`, not a branch name. Every such run therefore resolves to the same base directory. On any machine or self-hosted runner where that temp path persists between runs, `priorFindingsFor` (line 778) reads `round-N/<lens>/verdict.json` written while reviewing a *different* change and writes those findings into this round's `--prior-findings`, i.e. another branch's findings are re-raised as blockers here and fed into the verifier prompt; `nextRound` likewise inherits the other change's round count and can trip the 3-round bound (line 887) on a first round. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` has no `--symbolic-full-name`/`@{u}` fallback and there is no detached-HEAD guard anywhere in `cmdReview`.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts cmdReview passes raw `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` into reviewBase with "no detached-HEAD guard anywhere". The code does not read that way. At spec-to-pr.mjs:875 the abbrev output is passed through `branchKey(...)`, and `branchKey` (lines 755-764) explicitly rejects the literal "HEAD" (`if (name !== "" && name !== "HEAD") return name;`) and falls back to GITHUB_HEAD_REF, then GITHUB_REF_NAME (each rejected when empty or "HEAD"), then `detached-<sha12>`, then `detached-unknown`. The HEAD sha for that fallback is read at lines 871-874. Line 881 (`const requested = args.out ? path.resolve(args.out) : reviewBase(branch)`) is the only call site of reviewBase in the repo (grep for reviewBase|branchKey outside node_modules shows no other production caller), so no path reaches the round store keyed on the string "HEAD". Tests at spec-to-pr.test.mjs:678-697 assert each branch, including that two distinct detached shas produce distinct keys. The finding's cited line numbers (808, 723-727, 778, 887) also do not match the current file. The only residual collision is `detached-unknown` (line 763), which requires no HEAD commit and no CI ref — an unborn repository with nothing to review — not the claimed CI/rebase/bisect scenario.
